bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Learning to read charts with Volume Price Analysis is an intuitive art form rather than a mechanical science, relying on subjective human discretion and contextual comparison of price spread and wicks against relative volume history.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Principle No 1: Art Not Science The first principle to understand is that learning to read charts using VPA is an art, it is not a NOT a science.

facts.statement: VPA cannot be successfully automated through algorithmic software because programs lack subjectivity and cannot interpret the contextual subtleties required to compare candle spreads and wicks against relative volume history.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The reason software does not work with VPA, is simply that most of the analysis is subjective. You are comparing and analysing price behaviour against the associated volume... A software program, does not have any subjectivity.

facts.statement: The financial market behaves like a massive supertanker possessing immense momentum; it cannot stop or turn instantly, continuing to slide forward due to inertia when brakes or steering are applied.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Principle No 2 : Patience... The financial market is like a super tanker. It does not just stop and turn on a dime or sixpence. The market always has momentum and will almost always continue beyond the candle.

facts.statement: Just as a spill requires a second pass to fully absorb liquid after an initial wipe, the market undergoes a prolonged sideways consolidation phase during reversals to absorb all floating supply or demand before a trend can complete.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The market undergoes a prolonged mopping-up phase during sideways congestion to absorb all floating supply or demand before a reversal can complete.

facts.statement: Traders must never enter a position immediately upon seeing a single reversal candle or volume anomaly because a signal is only an early warning; patience is required to let the market finish its mopping-up operation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Never enter a position immediately upon seeing a single reversal candle or anomaly... A single signal is merely an early warning sign.

facts.statement: Absolute volume numbers are meaningless in VPA; traders must strictly evaluate whether a volume bar is low, average, high, or ultra-high relative to recent historical volume bars on the exact same chart feed.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Principle No 3 : It's All Relative... Volume evaluation is strictly relative. Traders do not measure absolute volume numbers; instead, they judge whether a volume bar is low, average, high, or ultra-high.

facts.statement: In VPA, traders constantly search for only two fundamental market conditions: Validation (where price spread and volume agree, confirming trend continuation) or Anomaly (where price and volume disagree, signaling a trap or reversal).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Principle No 6 : Validation or Anomaly In using VPA as our analytical approach, we are only ever looking for two things. Whether the price has been validated by the volume, or whether there is an anomaly.

facts.statement: A wide price spread accompanied by high or above-average volume represents valid bullish or bearish continuation, confirming that major institutional operators are actively participating in the trend.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wide Spread Candle: Large price spread + High / Above-average volume = Validation (Genuine move; major operators are participating in the trend).

facts.statement: A wide price spread occurring on low volume represents a major VPA anomaly—a fake move or insider trap where market makers mark prices up or down without real volume effort to test liquidity or trigger stops.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wide Spread Candle: Large price spread + Low / Below-average volume = Anomaly (Fake move / Insider Trap. Market makers are marking prices up/down without real volume).

facts.statement: A narrow price spread accompanied by high or ultra-high volume represents an absorption anomaly (wheels spinning on an icy hill), signaling heavy insider effort dumping inventory or absorbing opposing pressure ahead of a reversal.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Narrow Spread Candle: Small price spread + High / Ultra-high volume = Anomaly (Weakness / Absorption. High effort with little result... Insiders are dumping inventory).

facts.statement: VPA analysis follows a three-step hierarchical process: Micro (forensically analyzing each individual candle and volume bar), Macro (contextualizing against adjacent bars), and Global (evaluating full chart trend location and support/resistance zones).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Step 1 – Micro: Forensically analyze each individual price bar... Step 2 – Macro: Contextualize the current bar against adjacent bars... Step 3 – Global: Step back to evaluate the full chart.

facts.statement: VPA operates like a camera zoom lens in reverse—starting with close-up micro analysis on a single bar, zooming out to macro candle groups, and finally zooming out fully to the global chart context and broader market structure.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The camera zoom lens analogy: VPA operates like a camera zoom lens in reverse—starting close-up on a single bar, zooming out to local candle groups, and finally zooming out fully to the global chart context.

facts.statement: VPA must never be used in isolation; it requires integration with core technical tools such as support and resistance zones, trendlines, and chart patterns to provide spatial chart bearings.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Principle No 5 : Technical Analysis Context & Integration... VPA is not used in isolation. It must be integrated into broader technical analysis to provide spatial bearings on a chart.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
